evidence: books/peer-round-driver.lisp fn-prd-feed-action checked DEADLINE only while PHASE or OUTPUTP; host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-write-step set deadline nil when a command drained and fnn-feed-connected-step set it nil before the greeting. The :read/:offer arms then had no bound.
fix: fn-prd-feed-action: past DEADLINE with no retained input the action is :timeout. The host arms the wait with fn-prd-round-deadline when a command drains, after TCP completion (greeting) and after an implicit-TLS handshake; a complete reply clears it (a partial line does not). The timeout is a :read loss, so fn-feed-lost requeues the entry (K5: the reconnect re-offers by CHECK/IHAVE).
scenario: Peer accepts TCP, takes CHECK <a> (or the TAKETHIS article) and never answers (a hung innd, a paused server, a NAT path that dropped state after the ACK). The link reads :wait forever; the in-flight entry stays :offered/:sent; every later article for that peer queues behind it until the node restarts. Same for a peer that never sends its greeting.
title: Outbound feed waits for a peer's reply (and greeting) with no deadline: a hung or half-open peer holds its link and in-flight entry until restart
